_why: Example fleet-join recipe: copy to ~/.config/fleet/join.json and edit. Order matters: each step assumes the ones above it.

steps.name: homebrew
steps.say: install Homebrew (its installer asks for your password): https://brew.sh

steps.name: core packages
steps.check: for p in rsync gh jq syncthing coreutils; do /opt/homebrew/bin/brew list --versions $p >/dev/null || exit 1; done
steps.apply: /opt/homebrew/bin/brew install rsync gh jq syncthing coreutils

steps.name: syncthing mesh (tools, rules, registry)
steps.check: /opt/homebrew/bin/syncthing cli config folders list | grep -qx local-bin
steps.say: a Mac already in the fleet adds this Mac's device ID to ~/.local/state/mac-sync/mesh.sh and runs it on every Mac; then run it here

steps.name: shared tools
steps.say: arrive through the Syncthing local-bin folder

steps.name: fleet tools linked
steps.check: for t in tripwire idrive-ingest home-mirror utc-daily utc-schedule git-stale-locks fleet fleet-join; do test -e ~/.local/bin/$t || exit 1; done
steps.apply: for t in tripwire idrive-ingest home-mirror utc-daily utc-schedule git-stale-locks fleet fleet-join; do ln -sf ~/Projects/fleet/bin/$t ~/.local/bin/$t; done

steps.name: job
steps.check: launchctl print gui/$UID/{label} >/dev/null 2>&1 || launchctl print system/{label} >/dev/null 2>&1

steps.name: IDrive client signed in
steps.say: run `idrive-ingest login` on the hub and type the IDrive password yourself
